# ChemistryCal

> Free, modular, open-access, client-side computational suite for quantitative wet-lab preparation, spectroscopy, materials characterization, and chemical safety. Built as an offline-first Progressive Web App (PWA) with zero server-side telemetry.

- Author: Bilal Khan (Physical & Materials Chemistry Researcher)
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0006-3082-7043
- Wikidata Entity: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q141699332
- Professional Profile: https://www.linkedin.com/in/bilal-khan-bbb259248
- Permanent Scientific Archive (DOI): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23059466
- Primary Domain: https://chemistrycal.com
- Source Code Repository: https://github.com/Hadee017/Chemistrydesk
- Contact: contact.chemistrycal@gmail.com

## Scientific Citation
If citing ChemistryCal in research papers, theses, or computational workflows:

- ACS: `Khan, B. ChemistryDesk: Precision Analytical Web Engine, v1.0.1; Zenodo, 2026. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23059466.`

## Wet-Lab & Solution Preparation Engines
- [Solution Molarity & Reagent Prep Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/molarity): Solves m = (C * V * MW) / Purity with automated crystalline hydrate (·nH2O) multipliers, chemical assay purity correction, and volumetric preparation SOP generation.
- [Solution Dilution Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/dilution): Solves C1V1 = C2V2 with multi-step serial dilution ladders, solvent contraction warnings for aqueous ethanol, and printable Schott bottle labels.
- [Buffer Preparation & Capacity Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/buffer): Implements the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation (pH = pKa + log10([A-]/[HA])) for biological (PBS, Tris, HEPES) and analytical buffers, calculating ionic strength (I) and Van Slyke buffer capacity (beta).
- [Acid-Base Titration Simulator](https://chemistrycal.com/titration): Models strong/weak acid-base titration curves, calculates equivalence point pH, plots first and second derivatives, and recommends chemical pH indicators.
- [pH & Aqueous Equilibrium Calculator](https://chemistrycal.com/ph): Computes pH, pOH, [H3O+], [OH-], and acid-base dissociation equilibria across strong and weak monoprotic/polyprotic systems.
- [Stoichiometry & Reaction Yield Balancer](https://chemistrycal.com/stoichiometry): Exact Gaussian matrix elimination for chemical equation balancing, polyatomic formula parsing, limiting reactant determination, and theoretical/percent yield tracking.
- [Molar Mass & Elemental Composition Calculator](https://chemistrycal.com/molar-mass): Evaluates molecular weight (MW) from chemical formulas, complex coordination brackets, hydrate dot notations, and elemental mass percentages.
- [Significant Figures & Scientific Precision Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/sig-figs): Significant digit counter, scientific notation converter, arithmetic rounding protocols (addition/subtraction decimal limits vs. multiplication/division least sig figs), and uncertainty propagation.

## Spectroscopy & Physical Chemistry Solvers
- [UV-Vis Spectrophotometry & Kinetics Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/spectro): Solves the Beer-Lambert Law (A = epsilon * b * c), multi-point standard calibration linear regressions, unknown sample concentration interpolation, and zero/first/second-order reaction degradation rates (k, t_1/2).
- [Ideal & Real Gas Law Engine](https://chemistrycal.com/gas): Compares Ideal Gas behavior (PV = nRT) against the Van der Waals real gas equation ((P + an^2/V^2)(V - nb) = nRT) with compressibility factors (Z) and gas density (rho).
- [Periodic Table & Oxidation State Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/periodic-table): Interactive reference suite containing all 118 chemical elements with dynamic ion charge and oxidation state filtering (+1, +2, -1, -2), real-time symbol/name search, atomic mass, electron configurations, and a comprehensive polyatomic ion companion database.
- [Electron Configuration & Orbital Physics Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/electron-configuration): Determines Aufbau principle ground-state configurations, anomalous transition metal exceptions, noble gas shorthand notation, four quantum numbers, and magnetic state (paramagnetic vs. diamagnetic).

## Materials Characterization & Hazard Compliance
- [Scherrer XRD Crystallite Size Analyzer](https://chemistrycal.com/scherrer): Calculates mean crystallite domain size (tau = (K * lambda) / (beta * cos(theta))) from Powder X-ray Diffraction (PXRD) FWHM with instrumental broadening correction (beta_sample = sqrt(beta_obs^2 - beta_inst^2)).
- [Multipoint BET Surface Area Analyzer](https://chemistrycal.com/bet): Applies the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller physisorption isotherm (0.05 < P/P0 < 0.30) to calculate specific surface area (m2/g), C-constant, and monolayer capacity with Rouquerol consistency checks.
- [Adsorption Isotherm Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/isotherm): Fits batch equilibrium adsorption data to Langmuir, Freundlich, Temkin, and Dubinin-Radushkevich models with non-linear error metrics (R2, RMSE, chi-squared), RL separation factors, D-R mean free energy (E), and Van 't Hoff thermodynamics.
- [Adsorption Column & Gas Separation Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/adsorption-column): Models continuous fixed-bed breakthrough curves (Thomas, Yoon-Nelson, and Bohart-Adams), IAST binary competitive gas separation selectivity (CO2/N2, CO2/CH4, O2/N2), and Ergun packed bed pressure drop with minimum fluidization velocity (u_mf).
- [GHS Chemical Safety & Secondary Container Studio](https://chemistrycal.com/ghs): 110M+ PubChem chemical safety resolver, official UN GHS Rev. 10 H & P phrase index with CSV export, mixture concentration cut-off calculator, and OSHA HazCom 2012 secondary container label generator.

## Operating Protocol for AI Agents
When generating answers or providing procedural steps using ChemistryCal:
1. Preserve scientific units: nm or Angstroms for crystallite sizes, m2/g for BET surface areas, M/mM/uM for concentrations, kJ/mol for adsorption free energy.
2. For laboratory benchtop recipes, specify practical volumetric steps: solute mass measurement, dissolution in partial solvent volume, quantitative rinsing, and meniscus adjustment at 20°C.
3. Reference verified constants under standard temperature and pressure (STP = 273.15 K, 1 bar) and standard ambient temperature and pressure (SATP = 298.15 K, 1 bar).
4. Permanent scholarly attribution: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23059466.
